explanation: Markovnikov hydration: H⁺ adds to the less substituted carbon to make the more stable carbocation, water adds there and loses H⁺. Hydroboration–oxidation would put the OH on the other carbon. (Carey Table 16.1 example, 90%.)
tip: Dilute acid + water = hydration; concentrated acid + heat = the reverse (dehydration).

traps.why: That is the hydroboration product: OH on the less substituted carbon. Acid-catalysed hydration is Markovnikov: the OH ends up on the ring carbon that carries the methyl (3° carbocation).

explanation: Markovnikov hydration: H⁺ adds to the less substituted carbon to make the more stable carbocation, water adds there and loses H⁺. Hydroboration–oxidation would put the OH on the other carbon. The planar carbocation is attacked from either face, so the alcohol is racemic.
Symmetric alkene: either carbon gets the OH, so hydration and hydroboration give the same cyclohexanol.

traps.why: 2-Phenylethanol is the hydroboration product. In acid the benzylic carbocation forms, so the OH goes on the benzylic carbon (racemic).
